rfm_tuples.R: FY25 10-K Item 9B: 'On May 23, 2025, we entered into the Fifth Amendment to our Credit Facility... the minimum interest coverage ratio will be reduced from 1.55x to 1.00x to: (a) 1.15x... from the first quarter of fiscal 2026 through the third quarter of fiscal 2026; (b) 1.25x... from the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 through the first quarter of fiscal 2027; and (c) 1.55x... for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and thereafter.' Facility size 'permanently reduced from $600 million to $500 million.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify amendment exists; Mode B — quantify how close the company is to the relaxed covenant.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mode A confirmed. Mode B: This is the SECOND consecutive covenant-relief amendment (Fourth Amendment May 2024, Fifth Amendment May 2025) — covenant relief on top of covenant relief = chronic distress, not transitory. Q3 10-Q (12/27/25): cash $4.9M (DOWN from $20.8M at FY25 yearend), Long-term debt $45M, Total finance lease + financing obligations $240M, A/P $301M. Q3 9-month operating income only $25.2M vs $36.4M prior year (-31%). Q3 9-month interest expense $13.2M. TTM interest coverage proxy: (op income $25.2M + Q4 est ~$10M = ~$35M) / ($13.2M + Q4 est ~$4M = ~$17M) ~= 2.0x — comfortably above relaxed 1.15x threshold but well below the 1.55x normal covenant. The Fifth Amendment also required minimum $300M liquidity to declare dividends; the company is still paying $0.28/qtr dividend (~$8.7M/qtr declared Feb 13, 2026 8-K), so per its lender they have $300M+ liquidity. The $300M figure must be revolver availability against the $500M facility ($45M drawn → ~$455M available).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Recurring covenant relief is a real distress signal — Monro is structurally under-earning the original 1.55x interest-coverage covenant set by lenders. However, the issuer has not been forced to cut the dividend (kept at $0.28 for both Q3 and Q4 FY26), management asserts compliance, and the facility was right-sized ($600M → $500M). Not severe — the covenant relief shows lender willingness to accommodate the turnaround, which combined with Icahn's $84M bid is a coherent recovery setup. Mode B observation: the dividend persistence is itself a covenant-stress signal because the Fifth Amendment specifically modifies the dividend cushion (0.50x → 0.25x), meaning even lenders concede dividend headroom was binding.

summary: MNRO is a -28.8% drawdown forensic CONTRADICTION. The fundamentals are honestly impaired (three consecutive years of declining sales, FY25 GAAP net loss, 145-store closure, $14.8M closure charge, two consecutive covenant-relief amendments, $18.5M of AlixPartners turnaround fees, $736M goodwill exceeding total equity, dividends paid out of retained earnings) but the FORM-4 TAPE is the strongest LONG-bias signal in the forward-test universe: Carl Icahn deployed $84.7M open-market over Nov 4-7, 2025 to build a ~14.8% stake at avg $19.08, the company's NEW (March 2025) CEO Peter Fitzsimmons used $502K of personal cash to buy at $19 in Feb 2026 immediately after his permanent-CEO appointment, and the board responded to Icahn by adopting a 17.5%-trigger Rights Plan calibrated 2.7 pp above his then-current stake. ZERO open-market insider sales in the 12-month window — the four May 15, 2026 Form 4s clustering ten days before cutoff are all code-F tax-withholding on routine RSU vests (carefully disambiguated). Q3FY26 shows the first positive comparable-store-sales print (+1.2%) and operating income +87% YoY ($18.6M), validating the turnaround thesis Icahn is buying. Mode-B catches: (i) Rights Plan framed as generic shareholder protection is in fact a targeted Icahn pill; (ii) recurring covenant relief is chronic distress; (iii) $18.5M AlixPartners fee is material cash burn the 10-K does not foreground; (iv) goodwill carrying value at $736M against shareholders' equity of $605M is conditional on turnaround success. Verdict: LONG-tier. Insider conviction (Icahn $84.7M + CEO $502K + zero sells) plus a real Q3 fundamental inflection outweighs the entrenchment overhang.
